free_tier.stated: 'Most Semantic Scholar endpoints are available to the public without authentication, but they are rate-limited to 1000 requests per second shared among all unauthenticated users. Requests may also be further throttled during periods of heavy use.' An API key gives '1 RPS on all endpoints' as an introductory rate.
free_tier.notes: 1,000 requests/second is a pool shared by every anonymous caller in the world, not a per-client allowance.

per_object_cap.stated: batch lookup: 500 paper ids and up to 10 MB a call; relevance search: up to 1,000 results and 10 MB a call; bulk search: up to 1,000 papers a call with a continuation token and up to 10,000,000 papers in all

retention.stated: a continuously rebuilt index; no retention clock is published for the graph

egress.terms: Not metered by volume; no byte allowance is published. The key is a higher-limit credential, not a payment.
egress.free_allowance: 1,000 requests/second shared across all anonymous users

interface_detail: GET https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search?query=...&fields=...; x-api-key header when a key is used.
tooling: curl/python-requests; the semanticscholar python client; batch endpoints for up to 500 IDs per call.
chaining: The citation graph to join against Crossref and OpenAlex metadata; the shared anonymous pool makes it a best-effort enrichment step, not a bulk harvester.

limits.value: 1,000 requests/second shared among all unauthenticated users, further throttled under load; 1 RPS with an API key
batch: 500 paper ids and 10 MB a call; relevance search: 1,000 results; bulk search: 1,000 papers a call and 10,000,000 in all, beyond which the Datasets API applies

binding_note: The pool is shared with every keyless caller, so a caller's own rate does not decide access: a keyless search on 2026-10-31 answered 429 on the first call; a key gives a dedicated 1 request a second.

identity_cost.detail: Keyless calls are allowed but share one pool. The key comes from a request form that asks for first and last name, an email (academic or corporate requested), an affiliation and its website URL, country, a description of 50 words or more and the requests per day expected; the key is sent by email. No card. Whether every request is granted is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: The anonymous pool is exhausted often enough that a single first request returned 429 with a 174-byte JSON error; a harvester must treat 429 as the normal case rather than an exception.
confidence_note: The rate-limit sentence is the vendor's own, and a 429 was observed on the first anonymous request. The throughput at which 429s stop was not characterised.

evidence.proved: 'rate-limited to 1000 requests per second shared among all unauthenticated users' and '1 RPS on all endpoints' for a key
429 with 174 bytes of JSON on the first anonymous request - the shared pool was already exhausted
the key form asks for an academic or corporate email
evidence.quote: Please use an academic or corporate email.

evidence.proved: the key form asks for the affiliation's website URL
the key raises the rate limit; the page meters requests, not bytes
evidence.quote: Certain endpoints require authentication via an API key, and authenticated users have access to higher rate limits.

evidence.proved: a keyless paper search on 2026-10-31 answered 429 on the first call
the keyless 429 answer is a 174-byte JSON message that points to the key form
evidence.quote: Too Many Requests. Please wait and try again or apply for a key for higher rate limits.

evidence.proved: the batch endpoint takes at most 500 paper ids a call
evidence.quote: Can only process 500 paper ids at a time.

evidence.proved: bulk search stops at 10,000,000 papers; larger needs go to the Datasets API
evidence.quote: Up to 10,000,000 papers can be fetched via this method.

evidence.proved: a key gets 1 request a second on all endpoints
evidence.quote: The introductory rate limit for an API key is 1 RPS on all endpoints.

notes: The caveat is availability, not price: a 1,000 rps global pool sounds large and behaves like a queue. A key trades the pool for a predictable 1 rps.
